source.title: A Deeper Look at the Hessian Eigenspectrum of Deep Neural Networks and its Applications to Regularization
source.authors: A. R. Sankar; Yash Khasbage; Rahul Vigneswaran; Vineeth N. Balasubramanian

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present; some equation and figure formatting is flattened.
record.tranche_reason: Measures Hessian curvature during training and relates it to generalization error, then tests Hessian-trace regularization against generalization error. These are different measures and interventions from the claim versions’ specific experiments.
record.gate_note: Results on Hessian spectra and HTR bear on V7’s measured-property/generalization-gap relationship. HTR tables report generalization error but not training error or a train-test gap; they do not establish V1–V6 or V8. Cited results from prior work, including Keskar et al. (2017), are not this study’s own results. Figure-based curvature and training-accuracy findings are described in text, but precise values are unavailable.
record.test_reason: The study measures unscaled Hessian curvature and evaluates a new regularizer. It does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or compare its ranking of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures. Its own experiments do not test any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: layerwise Hessian spectra resemble the full-network spectrum, especially in middle layers; maximum eigenvalue and trace decrease during training; and HTR yields promising generalization improvements. The authors additionally report almost unchanged training accuracy, interpreting the test-error improvements as promising for reducing the generalization gap.
record.recipe_differences: Studies Hessian eigenspectra and introduces Hessian Trace Regularization; does not use the magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measurement in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The text reports that batch normalization reduces curvature and compares HTR on middle layers versus all layers; update frequency and regularization coefficient are varied, but the generalization-gap relation is not directly measured.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that Hessian trace decreases during training and is lower with architectural features associated with better generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian curvature can be associated with generalization performance in the tested architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: HTR lowers mean test error in Table 1; the authors report almost unchanged training accuracy and show training accuracy and reduced trace for LeNet on FashionMNIST in Figure 7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit Hessian-trace regularization can improve held-out performance with little change in training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Middle-layer HTR gives marginally lower mean test error than all-layer HTR, and combining HTR with L2 further lowers reported mean error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: HTR placement and combination with L2 affect its held-out performance.

record.problems: The curvature results are largely presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The generalization-error tables do not provide paired training errors or explicit train-test gaps, so they do not establish that Hessian measures track the gap named in V7.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were omitted. Cited prior-work results were excluded. Figure-only results for Hessian trace and eigenvalue trajectories are represented where the text supplies a result description; numerical values are unavailable.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout effects across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equal numbers of random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reason for excluding V7 is the mismatch in the measured construct, not simply missing numerical training errors. The text supplies qualitative training-accuracy comparisons, but these do not turn unscaled Hessian trace into magnitude-aware sharpness. No verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Batch-size effects on generalization under fixed epoch budgets.

The stated magnitude-aware perturbation measure and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. This paper studies Hessian curvature and regularization, not that specific measure. Its text reports a generalization-error connection but does not give paired train-test gaps for the measured curvature results.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

relation.reason: The paper discusses curvature and generalization, but does not test the specified magnitude-aware gap-tracking relation or use that particular finding as a tool.

tranche.reason: Unscaled Hessian curvature is a different construct from V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance. HTR performance comparisons do not test any other claim version.

source_check.notes: R2–R18 report the study's regularizer performance and placement comparisons; they are not eligible evidence for V1–V8. The text reports almost unchanged training accuracy and Figure 7 illustrates it, although numerical train–test gaps are not tabulated.
